title: Absolute file evidence resolves to its DEEPEST containing worktree, canonicalized, by exact path segment
context: dec_9ed4caea05 (now corrected/extended here) introduced deepestContainer/isWithin for absolute file evidence. Two further review rounds found and closed two more gaps in the same area: round 4 (mr-complexity-reviewer) found the existence check used bare existsSync, which is true for DIRECTORIES -- so a single directory-shaped evidence entry (or the natural '.'/"" an agent might send meaning 'the repo itself') silenced the guard for every OTHER entry in the same call, verified end-to-end through the real MCP server against a directory-shaped related_files entry this repo's own graph already carried (vscode-extension/). Round 5 found the containment hardening (deepestContainer/isWithin, rounds 3-4) had only ever applied to ABSOLUTE entries -- a RELATIVE entry containing a '..' segment that escapes root's own tree (e.g. '../<worktree>/only-in-worktree.ts', the IDENTICAL #54 misroute merely spelled relatively) bypassed containment entirely.
decision: existsUnder now checks isFile(f), never mere existsSync(f) -- a directory can never satisfy either the 'exists at root' escape hatch or a candidate match, closing the directory/empty-string bypass on the existence side (the git-history side of this same class is a separate decision, mcp.misroute-guard.history-check). misroutedWorktreeCandidates now pre-processes relatedFiles before any check: a relative entry is resolved against ROOT specifically (the only base the server actually has -- never re-resolved per candidate, which would answer a different, meaningless question) and promoted to an absolute entry ONLY if that resolution escapes root's own tree; a non-escaping relative entry keeps the original, intentional multi-location check (the same suffix tried at every candidate directory in turn) unchanged. A promoted (escaped) relative entry then runs through the identical deepestContainer/isFile logic an absolute entry gets.
consequences: A directory or empty-string entry (relative or absolute) now contributes nothing to either the existence check or the candidate search, closing the class of bug that let this repo's own vscode-extension/ related_files entry silence the guard
A relative "../<worktree>/x" spelling of the #54 misroute is now caught the same way the absolute spelling already was

A residual, DOCUMENTED gap remains: a non-escaping relative entry that happens to reach a worktree NESTED under root (e.g. '.worktrees/feature/x.ts', no '..' segment) still resolves as 'exists at root' via the plain join() check, since root's own directory tree DOES physically contain it -- this fails OPEN (silently uncaught), never toward a false positive, and full parity with the absolute case would need its own design pass
alternatives_rejected: Resolve EVERY relative entry to an absolute path up front (uniformly, not just escaping ones) and route all of them through deepestContainer alone -- rejected: this collapses the original, intentional 'try this relative suffix at every candidate directory' semantics into a single-location check, since a relative entry resolved once against root is lexically a DIFFERENT absolute path than the same relative entry resolved against a sibling worktree -- verified by execution that this breaks the plain sibling-worktree-by-relative-filename case #63 established

Fix only the reported case (a single '..' segment) rather than the general escape-detection -- rejected in favor of a general isWithin-based check that already handles multi-level escapes, redundant './.. ' segments, and escape-then-re-enter-root correctly with no special-casing
